Here's a concise implementation plan for `is_simple_power`:

• Handle edge cases: return `True` if `x == 1` (since any `n**0 = 1`), return `False` if `n <= 0`, `n == 1` (except when `x == 1`), or `x < 1`

• Use logarithms to find the potential exponent: calculate `exponent = log(x) / log(n)`, then check if `exponent` is close to an integer value (accounting for floating-point precision)

• Verify by computing `n ** round(exponent)` and checking if it equals `x` to confirm it's an exact power
